272	def _validate_one(
273	    connection_type: str, raw: dict[str, Any]
274	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, str | None]:
275	    """One suggestion through the same gate a human's `create_check` reaches.
276	    Returns (accepted suggestion, None) or (None, rejection reason).
277	    """
278	    expectation_type = raw.get("expectation_type")
279	    config = raw.get("config")
280	    if (
281	        not isinstance(expectation_type, str)
282	        or expectation_type not in SUGGESTIBLE_EXPECTATION_TYPES
283	    ):
284	        return None, f"expectation_type {expectation_type!r} is not in the offered vocabulary"
285	    if not isinstance(config, dict):
286	        return None, "config must be an object"
287	    try:
288	        check_service.validate_expectation_check(expectation_type, config)
289	        check_service.reject_dataframe_only_expectation(
290	            expectation_type, connection_type=connection_type
291	        )
292	    except check_service.CheckConfigInvalidError as exc:
293	        return None, exc.message
294	    dimension = check_dimension.derive_dimension(
295	        expectation_type=expectation_type, kind="expectation"
296	    )
297	    return {
298	        "expectation_type": expectation_type,
299	        "name": str(raw.get("name") or expectation_type)[:200],
300	        "rationale": str(raw.get("rationale") or "")[:500],
301	        "config": config,
302	        "dimension": dimension,
303	    }, None

306	def validate_output(
307	    session: Session, invocation: LlmInvocation, payload: dict[str, Any]
308	) -> dict[str, Any]:
309	    """Every suggestion rides `validate_expectation_check` before it is ever
310	    stored — an invalid one is dropped, not stored; a suggestion run that
311	    suggests nothing runnable is a hard failure, not an empty success.
312	    """
313	    suite = session.get(Suite, invocation.suite_id) if invocation.suite_id else None
314	    connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id) if suite is not None else None
315	    connection_type = connection.type if connection is not None else ""
316	    raw_suggestions = payload.get("suggestions")
317	    if not isinstance(raw_suggestions, list):
318	        raise LLMOutputInvalidError("provider did not return a suggestions list")
319	    accepted: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
320	    rejected: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
321	    for raw in raw_suggestions[:MAX_SUGGESTIONS]:
322	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
323	            rejected.append({"expectation_type": None, "reason": "suggestion was not an object"})
324	            continue
325	        ok, reason = _validate_one(connection_type, raw)
326	        if ok is not None:
327	            accepted.append(ok)
328	        else:
329	            rejected.append({"expectation_type": raw.get("expectation_type"), "reason": reason})
330	    if not accepted:
331	        raise LLMOutputInvalidError("no suggested check passed validation")
332	    return {"suggestions": accepted, "rejected": rejected}

137	    if connection.type == "unity_catalog" and not str(target.get("catalog") or "").strip():
138	        raise LLMRequestInvalidError("a Unity Catalog target requires a catalog")

141	def _profile_prompt(
142	    session: Session,
143	    suite: Suite,
144	    connection: Connection,
145	    *,
146	    secret_store: SecretStore,
147	    actor: uuid.UUID | None,
148	) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
149	    """Column names + masked profile stats. Refuses (rather than degrades) on
150	    failure: a suggestion grounded in nothing is a confident wrong answer —
151	    unlike #1512, the profile here is never optional, so no degrade path.
152	    """
153	    columns = llm_prompt_context.list_columns_for_prompt(
154	        session,
155	        suite,
156	        connection,
157	        secret_store=secret_store,
158	        actor=actor,
159	        consumer="llm_check_suggestion",
160	    )
161	    profile = llm_prompt_context.masked_profile_for_prompt(
162	        session,
163	        suite,
164	        connection,
165	        columns,
166	        top_n=_TOP_N,
167	        secret_store=secret_store,
168	        actor=actor,
169	        consumer="llm_check_suggestion",
170	    )
171	    lines = [f"Row count: {profile.row_count}"]
172	    for col in profile.columns:
173	        stats = [f"nulls={col.null_fraction:.1%}"]
174	        if col.distinct_count is not None:
175	            stats.append(f"distinct={col.distinct_count}")
176	        if col.min_value is not None or col.max_value is not None:
177	            stats.append(f"range=[{col.min_value}, {col.max_value}]")
178	        if col.top_values:
179	            top = ", ".join(f"{t.get('value')!r} x{t.get('count')}" for t in col.top_values)
180	            stats.append(f"top_values=[{top}]")
181	        lines.append(f"- {col.column}: {' '.join(stats)}")
182	    return "\n".join(lines), columns

185	def build_prompt(
186	    session: Session, invocation: LlmInvocation, secret_store: SecretStore
187	) -> tuple[str, str | None, dict[str, Any]]:
188	    suite = session.get(Suite, invocation.suite_id) if invocation.suite_id else None
189	    if suite is None:
190	        raise LLMRequestInvalidError("the suite this suggestion run was scoped to no longer exists")
191	    connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
192	    check_generation_preconditions(suite, connection)
193	    assert connection is not None  # preconditions refused None  # nosec B101
194	    actor = invocation.requested_by_user_id
195	    profile_text, columns = _profile_prompt(
196	        session, suite, connection, secret_store=secret_store, actor=actor
197	    )
198	    target = suite.target or {}
199	    qualified = ".".join(
200	        p for p in (target.get("catalog"), target.get("schema"), target.get("table")) if p
201	    )
202	    prompt = f"Table: {qualified}\nColumns: {', '.join(columns)}\n\nProfile:\n{profile_text}"
203	    return prompt, _SYSTEM, CHECKSUGGEST_SCHEMA

206	def _validate_one(
207	    connection_type: str, raw: dict[str, Any]
208	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, str | None]:
209	    """One suggestion through the same gate a human's `create_check` reaches.
210	    Returns (accepted suggestion, None) or (None, rejection reason).
211	    """
212	    expectation_type = raw.get("expectation_type")
213	    config = raw.get("config")
214	    if (
215	        not isinstance(expectation_type, str)
216	        or expectation_type not in SUGGESTIBLE_EXPECTATION_TYPES
217	    ):
218	        return None, f"expectation_type {expectation_type!r} is not in the offered vocabulary"
219	    if not isinstance(config, dict):
220	        return None, "config must be an object"
221	    try:
222	        check_service.validate_expectation_check(expectation_type, config)
223	        check_service.reject_dataframe_only_expectation(
224	            expectation_type, connection_type=connection_type
225	        )
226	    except check_service.CheckConfigInvalidError as exc:
227	        return None, exc.message
228	    dimension = check_dimension.derive_dimension(
229	        expectation_type=expectation_type, kind="expectation"
230	    )
231	    return {
232	        "expectation_type": expectation_type,
233	        "name": str(raw.get("name") or expectation_type)[:200],
234	        "rationale": str(raw.get("rationale") or "")[:500],
235	        "config": config,
236	        "dimension": dimension,
237	    }, None
238	
239	
240	def validate_output(
241	    session: Session, invocation: LlmInvocation, payload: dict[str, Any]
242	) -> dict[str, Any]:
243	    """Every suggestion rides `validate_expectation_check` before it is ever
244	    stored — an invalid one is dropped, not stored; a suggestion run that
245	    suggests nothing runnable is a hard failure, not an empty success.
246	    """
247	    suite = session.get(Suite, invocation.suite_id) if invocation.suite_id else None
248	    if suite is None:
249	        # Never fall back to a blank connection_type: reject_dataframe_only_expectation("",
250	        # ...) silently no-ops on an unknown type instead of refusing (#1719 review) — the
251	        # context vanishing is not the model's fault, same as build_prompt's own suite-gone
252	        # case, so this is request-invalid, not a validation failure of the model's output.
253	        raise LLMRequestInvalidError("the suite this suggestion run was scoped to no longer exists")
254	    connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
255	    if connection is None:
256	        raise LLMRequestInvalidError("the suite's connection no longer exists")
257	    connection_type = connection.type
258	    raw_suggestions = payload.get("suggestions")
259	    if not isinstance(raw_suggestions, list):
260	        raise LLMOutputInvalidError("provider did not return a suggestions list")
261	    accepted: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
262	    rejected: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
263	    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
264	    for raw in raw_suggestions[:MAX_SUGGESTIONS]:
265	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
266	            rejected.append({"expectation_type": None, "reason": "suggestion was not an object"})
267	            continue
268	        ok, reason = _validate_one(connection_type, raw)
269	        if ok is None:
270	            rejected.append({"expectation_type": raw.get("expectation_type"), "reason": reason})
271	            continue
272	        # The model can propose the same rule twice (a retry, or reasoning about
273	        # the same signal from two angles) — one accepted copy, not a duplicate
274	        # presented to the reviewer as two independently-validated suggestions.
275	        identity = (ok["expectation_type"], json.dumps(ok["config"], sort_keys=True, default=str))
276	        if identity in seen:
277	            rejected.append(
278	                {"expectation_type": ok["expectation_type"], "reason": "duplicate suggestion"}
279	            )
280	            continue
281	        seen.add(identity)
282	        accepted.append(ok)
283	    if not accepted:
284	        raise LLMOutputInvalidError("no suggested check passed validation")
285	    return {"suggestions": accepted, "rejected": rejected}

From the /code-review on #1719 (LLM curated check suggestions).

**Finding:** `llm_checksuggest._validate_one` validates a suggested check's `expectation_type` + `config` shape via `check_service.validate_expectation_check` (the same gate `create_check` uses), but nothing checks that `config["column"]` is actually one of the table's real columns. GX's pydantic construction only validates config *shape*, not column existence against the live schema.

**Why this isn't a regression, and isn't fixed in #1719:** `check_service.create_check` (the human/API/MCP authoring path) has the identical gap — it never checks column existence against the warehouse either. The check editor's UI dropdown is what prevents this in practice for humans; a hand-typed API/MCP `create_check` call can reference a nonexistent column today, same as a suggestion could. `validate_output` has no `secret_store` in its signature (the shared `KIND_VALIDATORS` contract other kinds also use), so re-listing columns at validation time isn't straightforward without a seam change.

**Failure scenario:** the model hallucinates or is adversarially steered toward a column name that isn't in the table (the prompt already documents this class of input as untrusted DATA, #1632). The suggestion passes validation, is returned as "validated," and if applied without a dry-run, saves cleanly and errors on every run.

**Suggested fix, scoped to the not-yet-built apply/review UI (deferred in #1719):** route "apply this suggestion" through the existing dry-run endpoint before save — exactly the step a careful human already takes, and the one place a live schema check is cheap because a live connection is already in hand.
EOF
)" --label enhancement --milestone "v1.2 Backlog" 2>&1

From two independent /code-review passes on #1719.

**Gap:** `profile_service._to_native`'s flat-file fallback renders a bytes value as `str(value)` (Python repr, e.g. `"b'\x01\x02'"`), while `jsonsafe.sanitize_json` (added in #1719, used by the SQL/warehouse profiling path and everywhere else results get JSONB-persisted) hex-encodes the same conceptual value (`"0102"`). **Not reachable today:** both LLM features that motivated the hex-encode fix (#1512 SQL generation, #1513 check suggestions) are gated to `SQL_QUERYABLE_TYPES` (Snowflake, Unity Catalog) via `check_generation_preconditions`, so `profile_connection` always takes the SQL path — `_to_native`'s flat-file fallback is never involved. Latent, not live.

**When it becomes live:** the moment flat-file/Iceberg support is added to either LLM feature (both modules' docstrings already flag this as a likely near-term follow-up), or any other surface profiles a flat-file BINARY-ish column and compares/displays it next to a SQL-sourced one.

**Suggested fix:** make `_to_native`'s bytes branch call `sanitize_json`'s bytes handling (or vice versa — route both through one shared bytes→hex helper) so a BINARY value renders identically regardless of datasource family.
EOF

fixup: unify preconditions/qualified-target, cover bytearray, report over-limit suggestions

/code-review round 3: three more findings, all confirmed by independent
review agents.

1. check_generation_preconditions and the catalog/schema/table qualified-
   name join were STILL duplicated between llm_sqlgen.py and
   llm_checksuggest.py even after llm_prompt_context.py's extraction —
   and the duplication had already drifted: llm_checksuggest's inline
   blank-check used truthiness while llm_sqlgen's _clean() only treated
   None as missing, so the same malformed target (e.g. {"table": 0})
   would be accepted by one feature and refused by the other. Both now
   share llm_prompt_context.check_sql_target_preconditions /
   .qualified_target, with only the per-feature message text varying.

2. sanitize_json's bytes fix didn't cover bytearray, which some DBAPI
   drivers return instead of bytes for a BINARY column — the identical
   TypeError this fix was written to close, just for the sibling type
   (core/artifacts.py and lineage/dbt_manifest.py already treat the two
   as a pair).

3. validate_output silently sliced off suggestions beyond MAX_SUGGESTIONS
   with raw_suggestions[:MAX_SUGGESTIONS] — a provider that doesn't
   strictly enforce the schema's maxItems could return more, and the
   excess never appeared in `rejected` despite the API docstring's claim
   that it explains "what didn't make it and why" for everything the
   model returned. Now every input item lands in exactly one of
   accepted/rejected.

Also moved the admin-user test fixture (identical across
test_llm_sqlgen.py/test_llm_checksuggest.py bar an email prefix) into
the shared llm_helpers.py, which exists for exactly this.

Filed #1721 (not fixed here): profile_service._to_native (flat-file)
and sanitize_json (SQL/warehouse) format a bytes value differently
(str-repr vs hex) — latent, since both LLM features are SQL-only in v1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

"""Prompt-injection adversarial battery (#1632), supporting #1512/#1513.

Posture (proven here, not assumed): output validation is the security boundary,
not prompt hygiene. Every test in this module either (a) proves a hostile string
reaches the assembled prompt as inert DATA in every context slot, or (b) proves
the output gate refuses a non-conforming result regardless of what produced it —
the per-feature output-gate batteries already living in test_llm_sqlgen.py /
test_llm_checksuggest.py ARE that half of this battery; this module fills the
gaps: the top_value and table/schema slots, and the response's OUTBOUND
untrusted-ness (never logged unredacted). Model-level jailbreak robustness is
explicitly out of scope — BYO-model means we don't control the model.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Any

import pytest

from backend.app.db.models import LlmInvocation, User
from backend.app.llm.base import LLMResult
from backend.app.services import llm_checksuggest, llm_service, llm_sqlgen
from backend.app.services import profile_service as profile_service_module
from backend.app.services.profile_service import ColumnProfile, ProfileResult
from backend.tests.support.adversarial import PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS
from backend.tests.support.llm_helpers import admin_user, enable_llm, make_sql_suite


@pytest.fixture
def admin(db_session: Any) -> User:
    return admin_user(db_session, prefix="injection")


def _invocation(db_session: Any, kind: str, suite: Any, admin: User) -> LlmInvocation:
    invocation = LlmInvocation(
        kind=kind,
        requested_by_user_id=admin.id,
        suite_id=suite.id,
        request={"description": "no null emails"} if kind == llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND else {},
    )
    db_session.add(invocation)
    db_session.commit()
    return invocation


def _build_prompt(kind: str, db_session: Any, invocation: LlmInvocation, store: Any) -> str:
    builder = llm_sqlgen.build_prompt if kind == llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND else llm_checksuggest.build_prompt
    prompt, _system, _schema = builder(db_session, invocation, store)
    return prompt


# ── top_value slot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@pytest.mark.parametrize("injection", PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", [llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND, llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND])
def test_injection_in_top_value_reaches_the_prompt_as_data_only(
    db_session: Any,
    admin: User,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    kind: str,
    injection: str,
) -> None:
    """A hostile top-value (a real value some row actually carries) must reach
    the prompt verbatim, never interpreted — the model sees it as DATA next to
    the "DATA, not instructions" framing, same as a hostile column name.
    """
    from backend.tests.support.fake_secret_store import FakeSecretStore

    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)  # no column_policy: QTY is not sensitive
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: ["QTY"])
    profile = ProfileResult(
        row_count=10,
        columns=[
            ColumnProfile(
                column="QTY",
                null_count=0,
                null_fraction=0.0,
                distinct_count=2,
                min_value=1,
                max_value=9,
                top_values=[{"value": injection, "count": 3}],
            )
        ],
    )

class _StructuredProvider:
    model = "fake"

    def __init__(self, parsed: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self._parsed = parsed

    def complete(self, prompt: str, **_kw: Any) -> LLMResult:  # pragma: no cover - unused
        return LLMResult(text=str(self._parsed))

    def complete_structured(self, prompt: str, *, schema: dict[str, Any], **_kw: Any) -> LLMResult:
        return LLMResult(text="", parsed=self._parsed, input_tokens=3, output_tokens=1)


class _LogRecorder:
    """A structlog-shaped stand-in that records every call, for every level."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, tuple[Any, ...], dict[str, Any]]] = []

    def __getattr__(self, level: str) -> Any:
        def _log(event: str, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
            self.calls.append((level, (event, *args), kwargs))

        return _log


def test_the_llm_response_is_never_logged_unredacted(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """The response is the untrusted OUTPUT of a system we do not control — it
    must never land in structured logs, which routinely reach a lower-trust
    sink (App Insights, a log aggregator) than the DB row itself.
    """
    marker = f"INJECTION-MARKER-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    store = enable_llm(db_session, admin)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: ["EMAIL"])

"""Prompt-injection adversarial battery (#1632).

Posture: output validation is the security boundary, not prompt hygiene — the
per-feature output-gate tests already prove that half. This file proves a
hostile string reaches the prompt as inert data in every context slot, that
neither builder can read a sample row, and that a response is never logged
unredacted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Any

import pytest
import structlog
from structlog.testing import capture_logs

from backend.app.db.models import LlmInvocation, User
from backend.app.llm.base import LLMResult
from backend.app.services import llm_checksuggest, llm_service, llm_sqlgen
from backend.app.services import profile_service as profile_service_module
from backend.app.services.profile_service import ColumnProfile, ProfileResult
from backend.tests.support.adversarial import PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS
from backend.tests.support.fake_secret_store import FakeSecretStore
from backend.tests.support.llm_helpers import admin_user, make_sql_suite

_KINDS = [llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND, llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND]


@pytest.fixture
def admin(db_session: Any) -> User:
    return admin_user(db_session, prefix="injection")


def _invocation(db_session: Any, kind: str, suite: Any, admin: User) -> LlmInvocation:
    invocation = LlmInvocation(
        kind=kind,
        requested_by_user_id=admin.id,
        suite_id=suite.id,
        request={"description": "no null emails"} if kind == llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND else {},
    )
    db_session.add(invocation)
    db_session.commit()
    return invocation


def _build_prompt(kind: str, db_session: Any, invocation: LlmInvocation, store: Any) -> str:
    builder = (
        llm_sqlgen.build_prompt if kind == llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND else llm_checksuggest.build_prompt
    )
    prompt, _system, _schema = builder(db_session, invocation, store)
    return prompt


def _empty_profile(column: str) -> ProfileResult:
    return ProfileResult(
        row_count=1,
        columns=[
            ColumnProfile(
                column=column,
                null_count=0,
                null_fraction=0.0,
                distinct_count=1,
                min_value=None,
                max_value=None,
                top_values=[],
            )
        ],
    )


# ── column name slot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@pytest.mark.parametrize("injection", PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", _KINDS)
def test_injection_in_column_name_reaches_the_prompt_as_data_only(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, kind: str, injection: str
) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: [injection])
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        profile_service_module, "profile_connection", lambda *_a, **_kw: _empty_profile(injection)
    )
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, kind, suite, admin)
    if kind == llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND:
        invocation.request = {**(invocation.request or {}), "include_profile": True}
        db_session.commit()

    prompt = _build_prompt(kind, db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore())
    assert injection in prompt


# ── top_value and range slots (checksuggest only — sql-gen's top_n=0 posture ──
# means neither ever reaches its prompt at all) ──────────────────────────────


@pytest.mark.parametrize("injection", PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS)
def test_injection_in_top_value_reaches_the_checksuggest_prompt_as_data_only(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, injection: str
) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)  # no column_policy: QTY is not sensitive
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: ["QTY"])
    profile = ProfileResult(
        row_count=10,
        columns=[
            ColumnProfile(
                column="QTY",
                null_count=0,
                null_fraction=0.0,
                distinct_count=2,
                min_value=1,
                max_value=9,
                top_values=[{"value": injection, "count": 3}],
            )
        ],
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "profile_connection", lambda *_a, **_kw: profile)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND, suite, admin)

    prompt = _build_prompt(
        llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND, db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore()
    )
    # rendered via repr() — quoted/escape-visible, but must still carry the string.
    assert repr(injection) in prompt


@pytest.mark.parametrize("injection", PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS)
def test_injection_in_column_range_reaches_the_checksuggest_prompt_as_data_only(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, injection: str
) -> None:
    """min_value/max_value (a text column's lexical MIN/MAX) render via a bare
    f-string, unlike top_values — a distinct slot from the same warehouse trust
    class and worth its own proof.
    """
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: ["CODE"])
    profile = ProfileResult(
        row_count=5,
        columns=[
            ColumnProfile(
                column="CODE",
                null_count=0,
                null_fraction=0.0,
                distinct_count=5,
                min_value=injection,
                max_value="z",
                top_values=[],
            )
        ],
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "profile_connection", lambda *_a, **_kw: profile)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND, suite, admin)

    prompt = _build_prompt(
        llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND, db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore()
    )
    assert injection in prompt


# ── table / schema name slot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────


@pytest.mark.parametrize("injection", PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS)
def test_injection_in_table_name_reaches_sqlgen_prompt_as_data_only(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, injection: str
) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin, target={"table": injection, "schema": "RETAIL"})
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: ["ID"])
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND, suite, admin)

    prompt = _build_prompt(llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND, db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore())
    # target fields are whitespace-stripped (`_clean()`) before assembly.
    assert injection.strip() in prompt


@pytest.mark.parametrize("injection", PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS)
def test_injection_in_schema_name_reaches_checksuggest_prompt_as_data_only(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, injection: str
) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin, target={"table": "ORDERS", "schema": injection})
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: ["ID"])
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        profile_service_module, "profile_connection", lambda *_a, **_kw: _empty_profile("ID")
    )
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND, suite, admin)

    prompt = _build_prompt(
        llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND, db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore()
    )
    assert injection.strip() in prompt


# ── PII discipline: structural, not incidental ───────────────────────────────


def test_neither_builder_touches_result_or_sample_failures() -> None:
    """No raw sample row can reach a prompt if `Result` is never even imported —
    a structural guarantee, not an incidental one (the #849 lesson: test the
    pipeline, not a scrub helper that could be bypassed).
    """
    import inspect

    for module in (llm_sqlgen, llm_checksuggest):
        assert "sample_failures" not in inspect.getsource(module)
        assert not hasattr(module, "Result")


# ── outbound: the response is untrusted too ──────────────────────────────────


class _StructuredProvider:
    model = "fake"

    def __init__(self, parsed: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self._parsed = parsed

    def complete(self, prompt: str, **_kw: Any) -> LLMResult:  # pragma: no cover - unused
        return LLMResult(text=str(self._parsed))

    def complete_structured(self, prompt: str, *, schema: dict[str, Any], **_kw: Any) -> LLMResult:
        return LLMResult(text="", parsed=self._parsed, input_tokens=3, output_tokens=1)


def _sqlgen_payload(marker: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"sql": f"SELECT '{marker}'", "explanation": marker}


def _checksuggest_payload(marker: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "suggestions": [
            {
                "expectation_type": "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
                "name": marker,
                "rationale": marker,
                "config": {"column": "EMAIL"},
            }
        ]
    }


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "kind, payload_for",
    [(llm_sqlgen.SQLGEN_KIND, _sqlgen_payload), (llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND, _checksuggest_payload)],
)
def test_the_response_is_never_logged_unredacted(
    db_session: Any,
    admin: User,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    kind: str,
    payload_for: Any,
) -> None:
    """The response is the untrusted OUTPUT of a system we do not control — it
    must never land in structured logs, which routinely reach a lower-trust
    sink than the DB row itself.
    """
    marker = f"INJECTION-MARKER-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: ["EMAIL"])
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        profile_service_module, "profile_connection", lambda *_a, **_kw: _empty_profile("EMAIL")
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        llm_service, "build_provider", lambda *_a, **_kw: _StructuredProvider(payload_for(marker))
    )
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, kind, suite, admin)

    with capture_logs() as logs:
        monkeypatch.setattr(llm_service, "log", structlog.get_logger("backend.app.services.llm_service"))
        status = llm_service.execute_invocation(db_session, invocation.id, secret_store=FakeSecretStore())

    assert status == "succeeded"
    db_session.refresh(invocation)
    assert marker in str(invocation.response)  # sanity: the response was actually used
    assert logs, "no log calls captured — the assertion above would be vacuous"
    assert marker not in str(logs)

fixup: close column/range slot gaps, harden the structural guard, dedupe log capture

    #: A deterministic default threshold, for when no LLM is configured — the
    #: largest observed gap plus margin, not the median: a threshold tighter
    #: than the slowest still-healthy cycle would false-positive on it.
    suggested_fail_threshold_hours: float | None = None


def compute_pipeline_cadence(
    session: Session, *, provider: str, pipeline_or_dag_id: str, env: str
) -> PipelineCadence:
    rows = session.execute(
        select(func.coalesce(PipelineRun.started_at, PipelineRun.created_at))
        .where(
            PipelineRun.provider == provider,
            PipelineRun.pipeline_or_dag_id == pipeline_or_dag_id,
            PipelineRun.env == env,
            PipelineRun.status == "succeeded",
        )
        .order_by(func.coalesce(PipelineRun.started_at, PipelineRun.created_at).desc())
        .limit(_CADENCE_HISTORY_LIMIT)
    ).all()
    timestamps = sorted(r[0] for r in rows)
    if len(timestamps) < _CADENCE_MIN_RUNS:
        return PipelineCadence(sample_count=len(timestamps), insufficient_history=True)
    gaps_hours = sorted(
        (later - earlier).total_seconds() / 3600
        for earlier, later in zip(timestamps, timestamps[1:], strict=False)
    )
    mid = len(gaps_hours) // 2
    median = gaps_hours[mid] if len(gaps_hours) % 2 else (gaps_hours[mid - 1] + gaps_hours[mid]) / 2
    max_gap = gaps_hours[-1]
    return PipelineCadence(
        sample_count=len(timestamps),
        insufficient_history=False,
        median_gap_hours=round(median, 2),
        max_gap_hours=round(max_gap, 2),
        suggested_fail_threshold_hours=round(max_gap * 1.25, 1),
    )

"""compute_pipeline_cadence (#1648): inter-run gaps grounding a freshness suggestion."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

from backend.app.db.models import Connection, PipelineRun, User
from backend.app.services.orchestration_service import compute_pipeline_cadence

NOW = datetime(2026, 6, 29, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)


def _connection(db_session: Any) -> Connection:
    user = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"u-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com")
    db_session.add(user)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}", type="airflow", env="dev", config={}, created_by=user.id
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.commit()
    return conn


def _run(db_session: Any, conn: Connection, *, hours_ago: float, status: str = "succeeded") -> None:
    started = NOW - timedelta(hours=hours_ago)
    db_session.add(
        PipelineRun(
            provider="airflow",
            connection_id=conn.id,
            provider_run_id=f"run-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
            pipeline_or_dag_id="load_orders",
            env="dev",
            status=status,
            started_at=started,
            finished_at=started + timedelta(minutes=5),
            created_at=started,
        )
    )


def _cadence(db_session: Any):
    return compute_pipeline_cadence(
        db_session, provider="airflow", pipeline_or_dag_id="load_orders", env="dev"
    )


def test_insufficient_history_below_the_minimum_run_count(db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    _run(db_session, conn, hours_ago=2)
    _run(db_session, conn, hours_ago=1)  # only 2 succeeded runs — below the min
    db_session.commit()

    cadence = _cadence(db_session)

    assert cadence.insufficient_history is True
    assert cadence.sample_count == 2
    assert cadence.median_gap_hours is None
    assert cadence.suggested_fail_threshold_hours is None


def test_regular_cadence_computes_median_and_a_margined_default(db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    # Four runs, evenly spaced 6 hours apart.
    for hours_ago in (18, 12, 6, 0):
        _run(db_session, conn, hours_ago=hours_ago)
    db_session.commit()

    cadence = _cadence(db_session)

    assert cadence.insufficient_history is False
    assert cadence.sample_count == 4
    assert cadence.median_gap_hours == 6.0
    assert cadence.max_gap_hours == 6.0
    # Deterministic fallback: margined above the worst observed gap, not tight to it.
    assert cadence.suggested_fail_threshold_hours == 7.5


def test_an_irregular_gap_widens_the_max_but_not_the_median(db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    # Mostly 4h apart, one outlier 20h gap.
    for hours_ago in (28, 8, 4, 0):
        _run(db_session, conn, hours_ago=hours_ago)
    db_session.commit()

    cadence = _cadence(db_session)

    assert cadence.median_gap_hours == 4.0
    assert cadence.max_gap_hours == 20.0
    assert cadence.suggested_fail_threshold_hours == 25.0


def test_failed_runs_are_excluded_from_the_cadence(db_session: Any) -> None:
    """A failed run produced no new data — it must not count as an arrival."""
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    for hours_ago in (12, 8, 4, 0):
        _run(db_session, conn, hours_ago=hours_ago, status="succeeded")
    _run(db_session, conn, hours_ago=2, status="failed")  # would shrink the gap if counted
    db_session.commit()

    cadence = _cadence(db_session)

    assert cadence.sample_count == 4
    assert cadence.median_gap_hours == 4.0


def test_a_different_pipeline_or_env_does_not_contaminate_the_cadence(db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    for hours_ago in (12, 8, 4, 0):
        _run(db_session, conn, hours_ago=hours_ago)
    # A same-connection run for a DIFFERENT dag, and one in a different env.
    db_session.add(
        PipelineRun(
            provider="airflow",
            connection_id=conn.id,
            provider_run_id="other-dag",
            pipeline_or_dag_id="load_payments",
            env="dev",
            status="succeeded",
            started_at=NOW,
            created_at=NOW,
        )
    )
    db_session.add(
        PipelineRun(
            provider="airflow",
            connection_id=conn.id,
            provider_run_id="other-env",
            pipeline_or_dag_id="load_orders",
            env="qa",
            status="succeeded",
            started_at=NOW,
            created_at=NOW,
        )
    )
    db_session.commit()

    cadence = _cadence(db_session)

    assert cadence.sample_count == 4


def test_no_history_at_all(db_session: Any) -> None:
    cadence = compute_pipeline_cadence(
        db_session, provider="airflow", pipeline_or_dag_id="never_run", env="dev"
    )
    assert cadence.insufficient_history is True
    assert cadence.sample_count == 0

236	    stored — an invalid one is dropped, not stored; a suggestion run that

238	    """

245	        raise LLMRequestInvalidError("the suite this suggestion run was scoped to no longer exists")

251	    if not isinstance(raw_suggestions, list):
252	        raise LLMOutputInvalidError("provider did not return a suggestions list")

254	    rejected: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
255	    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
256	    for raw in raw_suggestions:
257	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
258	            rejected.append({"expectation_type": None, "reason": "suggestion was not an object"})

261	        # enforces its own schema server-side — an over-long response is
262	        # reported, not silently sliced off (every input item lands in exactly
263	        # one of accepted/rejected). Checked after the shape check so a
264	        # malformed item past the cap still reports its real defect.
265	        if len(accepted) >= MAX_SUGGESTIONS:
266	            rejected.append(
267	                {
268	                    "expectation_type": raw.get("expectation_type"),
269	                    "reason": "suggestion limit reached",
270	                }
271	            )
272	            continue
273	        ok, reason = _validate_one(connection_type, raw)
274	        if ok is None:
275	            rejected.append({"expectation_type": raw.get("expectation_type"), "reason": reason})
276	            continue
277	        # The model can propose the same rule twice (a retry, or reasoning about
278	        # the same signal from two angles) — one accepted copy, not a duplicate
279	        # presented to the reviewer as two independently-validated suggestions.
280	        identity = (ok["expectation_type"], json.dumps(ok["config"], sort_keys=True, default=str))
281	        if identity in seen:
282	            rejected.append(
283	                {"expectation_type": ok["expectation_type"], "reason": "duplicate suggestion"}
284	            )
285	            continue
286	        seen.add(identity)
287	        accepted.append(ok)
288	    if not accepted:
289	        raise LLMOutputInvalidError("no suggested check passed validation")
290	    return {"suggestions": accepted, "rejected": rejected}

"""Cadence-aware check suggestions (#1648): trigger-binding cadence context,
the monitor:freshness suggestion path, and orchestration coverage warnings.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

import pytest

from backend.app.db.models import Connection, LlmInvocation, PipelineRun, Suite, TriggerBinding, User
from backend.app.llm.base import LLMOutputInvalidError
from backend.app.services import llm_checksuggest
from backend.app.services import profile_service as profile_service_module
from backend.app.services.profile_service import ColumnProfile, ProfileResult
from backend.tests.support.fake_secret_store import FakeSecretStore
from backend.tests.support.llm_helpers import admin_user, make_sql_suite

NOW = datetime(2026, 6, 29, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)


@pytest.fixture
def admin(db_session: Any) -> User:
    return admin_user(db_session, prefix="cadence")


def _invocation(db_session: Any, suite: Suite, admin: User) -> LlmInvocation:
    invocation = LlmInvocation(
        kind=llm_checksuggest.CHECKSUGGEST_KIND, requested_by_user_id=admin.id, suite_id=suite.id
    )
    db_session.add(invocation)
    db_session.commit()
    return invocation


def _binding(db_session: Any, suite: Suite, *, env: str = "dev", enabled: bool = True) -> TriggerBinding:
    binding = TriggerBinding(
        provider="airflow",
        pipeline_or_dag_id="load_orders",
        env=env,
        suite_id=suite.id,
        enabled=enabled,
    )
    db_session.add(binding)
    db_session.commit()
    return binding


def _succeeded_run(db_session: Any, conn: Connection, *, hours_ago: float, env: str = "dev") -> None:
    started = NOW - timedelta(hours=hours_ago)
    db_session.add(
        PipelineRun(
            provider="airflow",
            connection_id=conn.id,
            provider_run_id=f"run-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
            pipeline_or_dag_id="load_orders",
            env=env,
            status="succeeded",
            started_at=started,
            finished_at=started + timedelta(minutes=2),
            created_at=started,
        )
    )


def _orchestration_connection(db_session: Any, admin: User) -> Connection:
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"orch-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}", type="airflow", env="dev", config={}, created_by=admin.id
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.commit()
    return conn


def _empty_profile(column: str) -> ProfileResult:
    return ProfileResult(
        row_count=1,
        columns=[
            ColumnProfile(
                column=column,
                null_count=0,
                null_fraction=0.0,
                distinct_count=1,
                min_value=None,
                max_value=None,
                top_values=[],
            )
        ],
    )


def _mock_profile(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, column: str = "EMAIL") -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(profile_service_module, "list_columns", lambda *_a, **_kw: [column])
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        profile_service_module, "profile_connection", lambda *_a, **_kw: _empty_profile(column)
    )


# ── build_prompt: cadence context ────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_no_binding_offers_no_freshness_type(db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    _mock_profile(monkeypatch)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    prompt, system, schema = llm_checksuggest.build_prompt(
        db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore()
    )

    assert "Pipeline cadence" not in prompt
    assert llm_checksuggest.FRESHNESS_EXPECTATION_TYPE not in schema["properties"]["suggestions"][
        "items"
    ]["properties"]["expectation_type"]["enum"]
    assert "freshness" not in system.lower()


def test_binding_with_insufficient_history_stays_freshness_free(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: Any
) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    orch_conn = _orchestration_connection(db_session, admin)
    _binding(db_session, suite)
    _succeeded_run(db_session, orch_conn, hours_ago=1)  # only 1 run — below the minimum
    db_session.commit()
    _mock_profile(monkeypatch)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    prompt, _system, schema = llm_checksuggest.build_prompt(
        db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore()
    )

    assert "insufficient history" in prompt
    assert llm_checksuggest.FRESHNESS_EXPECTATION_TYPE not in schema["properties"]["suggestions"][
        "items"
    ]["properties"]["expectation_type"]["enum"]


def test_binding_with_regular_cadence_offers_freshness_and_states_the_gap(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: Any
) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    orch_conn = _orchestration_connection(db_session, admin)
    _binding(db_session, suite)
    for hours_ago in (12, 8, 4, 0):
        _succeeded_run(db_session, orch_conn, hours_ago=hours_ago)
    db_session.commit()
    _mock_profile(monkeypatch)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    prompt, system, schema = llm_checksuggest.build_prompt(
        db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore()
    )

    assert "median=4.0h" in prompt
    assert llm_checksuggest.FRESHNESS_EXPECTATION_TYPE in schema["properties"]["suggestions"][
        "items"
    ]["properties"]["expectation_type"]["enum"]
    assert llm_checksuggest.FRESHNESS_EXPECTATION_TYPE in system


def test_a_disabled_binding_is_not_used(db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    orch_conn = _orchestration_connection(db_session, admin)
    _binding(db_session, suite, enabled=False)
    for hours_ago in (12, 8, 4, 0):
        _succeeded_run(db_session, orch_conn, hours_ago=hours_ago)
    db_session.commit()
    _mock_profile(monkeypatch)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    prompt, _system, _schema = llm_checksuggest.build_prompt(
        db_session, invocation, FakeSecretStore()
    )

    assert "Pipeline cadence" not in prompt


# ── output gate: monitor:freshness suggestions ───────────────────────────────


def _freshness_suggestion(**overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    base = {
        "expectation_type": llm_checksuggest.FRESHNESS_EXPECTATION_TYPE,
        "name": "orders freshness",
        "rationale": "cadence shows ~4h between loads",
        "config": {"column": "LOADED_AT"},
        "fail_threshold_hours": 8,
    }
    base.update(overrides)
    return base


def test_output_gate_accepts_a_valid_freshness_suggestion(db_session: Any, admin: User) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    out = llm_checksuggest.validate_output(
        db_session, invocation, {"suggestions": [_freshness_suggestion()]}
    )

    assert len(out["suggestions"]) == 1
    accepted = out["suggestions"][0]
    assert accepted["expectation_type"] == "monitor:freshness"
    assert accepted["dimension"] == "timeliness"
    assert accepted["fail_threshold_hours"] == 8.0


def test_output_gate_rejects_a_freshness_suggestion_with_no_positive_threshold(
    db_session: Any, admin: User
) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    out = llm_checksuggest.validate_output(
        db_session,
        invocation,
        {"suggestions": [_freshness_suggestion(fail_threshold_hours=None)]},
    )

    assert out["suggestions"] == []  # falls through to "coverage_warnings" below
    assert len(out["rejected"]) == 1
    assert "threshold" in out["rejected"][0]["reason"]


def test_output_gate_rejects_a_freshness_suggestion_missing_a_column(
    db_session: Any, admin: User
) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)  # snowflake — needs a column, no arrival-time
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    with pytest.raises(LLMOutputInvalidError):
        llm_checksuggest.validate_output(
            db_session, invocation, {"suggestions": [_freshness_suggestion(config={})]}
        )


def test_output_gate_rejects_a_negative_freshness_threshold(db_session: Any, admin: User) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    out = llm_checksuggest.validate_output(
        db_session,
        invocation,
        {"suggestions": [_freshness_suggestion(fail_threshold_hours=-1)]},
    )

    assert out["suggestions"] == []
    assert len(out["rejected"]) == 1


# ── coverage_warnings: deterministic, independent of what the model returns ──


def test_coverage_warnings_is_empty_with_no_near_miss(db_session: Any, admin: User) -> None:
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    out = llm_checksuggest.validate_output(
        db_session,
        invocation,
        {"suggestions": [_freshness_suggestion()]},
    )

    assert out["coverage_warnings"] == []


def test_coverage_warnings_surfaces_a_real_near_miss(db_session: Any, admin: User) -> None:
    """A binding scoped to 'dev' whose pipeline ALSO succeeds in 'qa' (no binding
    there) is exactly the #1199 near-miss shape (env mismatch) reused as a
    coverage warning for this suite.
    """
    suite = make_sql_suite(db_session, admin)
    orch_conn = _orchestration_connection(db_session, admin)
    _binding(db_session, suite, env="dev")
    _succeeded_run(db_session, orch_conn, hours_ago=1, env="qa")
    db_session.commit()
    from backend.app.services import workspace_health_service

    workspace_health_service.record_trigger_binding_env_near_miss(
        db_session, provider="airflow", pipeline_or_dag_id="load_orders", run_env="qa", binding_env="dev"
    )
    invocation = _invocation(db_session, suite, admin)

    out = llm_checksuggest.validate_output(
        db_session, invocation, {"suggestions": [_freshness_suggestion()]}
    )

    assert len(out["coverage_warnings"]) == 1
    warning = out["coverage_warnings"][0]
    assert warning["run_env"] == "qa"
    assert warning["binding_env"] == "dev"

## Summary
Extends #1513's check-suggestion builder — same seam, no new invocation kind.

- **`orchestration_service.compute_pipeline_cadence`**: median/max inter-run gap over a bound pipeline's own succeeded-run history (`pipeline_runs`), plus a deterministic margined-default threshold (max gap × 1.25) that needs no LLM at all. Below 3 runs, labeled `insufficient_history`, never asserted — the explicit honesty rule the issue calls for.
- **`build_prompt`** looks up the suite's enabled trigger binding (if any) and only offers `monitor:freshness` in the structured-output schema when the cadence is actually grounded. No binding, or insufficient history → unchanged GX-only behavior (verified: existing #1513 tests all still pass untouched).
- A `monitor:freshness` suggestion rides `validate_monitor_check` + `validate_threshold_ordering` — the same gates `create_check` reaches for a human-authored freshness monitor (SQL-connection column requirement, positive-threshold requirement).
- **Coverage warnings**: reuses the existing #1199 near-miss machinery (a pipeline succeeding in an env with no binding) rather than reinventing it, surfaced as a deterministic `coverage_warnings` response field computed independently of what the model returns.

**Deliberately deferred, matching #1512/#1513's own precedent**: the check-editor UI hint for the deterministic fallback. The cadence computation itself needs no LLM and is ready for that hint; wiring it into the check editor is a separate frontend change.

## Test plan

def _owner_b_e_suite(db_session: Any) -> tuple[User, User, User, str]:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email="owner@ex")
    b = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email="b@ex")
    e = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email="e@ex")  # no access
    db_session.add_all([owner, b, e])
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "x"},
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.flush()
    suite = Suite(name="s", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)
    db_session.add(suite)
    db_session.commit()
    return owner, b, e, str(suite.id)

def _succeeded_run(db_session: Any, conn: Connection, *, hours_ago: float, env: str = "dev") -> None:
    started = datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=hours_ago)
    db_session.add(

            connection_id=conn.id,
            provider_run_id=f"run-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
            pipeline_or_dag_id="load_orders",
            env=env,
            status="succeeded",
            started_at=started,
            finished_at=started + timedelta(minutes=2),
            created_at=started,
        )
    )

    owner, _b, _e, sid = _owner_b_e_suite(db_session)

        "provider": None,

        "env": None,

        "insufficient_history": True,
        "median_gap_hours": None,
        "max_gap_hours": None,
        "suggested_fail_threshold_hours": None,
    }


def test_cadence_with_a_bound_pipeline_and_regular_history(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    owner, _b, _e, sid = _owner_b_e_suite(db_session)
    orch_conn = _orchestration_connection(db_session, "airflow")
    db_session.add(
        TriggerBinding(
            provider="airflow", pipeline_or_dag_id="load_orders", env="dev", suite_id=uuid.UUID(sid)
        )
    )
    for hours_ago in (12, 8, 4, 0):
        _succeeded_run(db_session, orch_conn, hours_ago=hours_ago)
    db_session.commit()
    _as(owner)

    resp = client.get(f"/api/v1/suites/{sid}/cadence")

    assert resp.status_code == 200
    body = resp.json()
    assert body["bound"] is True
    assert body["provider"] == "airflow"
    assert body["pipeline_or_dag_id"] == "load_orders"
    assert body["insufficient_history"] is False
    assert body["sample_count"] == 4
    assert body["median_gap_hours"] == 4.0

input.new_string:
def get_enabled_binding(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID) -> TriggerBinding | None:
    """A suite's most recently created enabled binding, or `None`. A suite can
    legitimately have more than one (two pipelines both triggering it) — this
    is for the single-binding consumers (a cadence hint, the LLM suggestion
    prompt), which need a deterministic pick, newest first, rather than
    whichever row Postgres happens to return. `id` breaks a `created_at` tie —
    `now()` is transaction-start time, not per-statement, so two bindings
    created in the same request-scoped transaction DO tie (mirrors
    `pipeline_run_order_by`'s identical reasoning).
    """
    return session.scalars(
        select(TriggerBinding)
        .where(TriggerBinding.suite_id == suite_id, TriggerBinding.enabled.is_(True))
        .order_by(TriggerBinding.created_at.desc(), TriggerBinding.id.desc())
    ).first()

def test_two_enabled_bindings_pick_stays_stable_across_calls(
    db_session: Any, admin: User, monkeypatch: Any
) -> None:
    """A suite can legitimately have more than one enabled binding. `created_at`
    is transaction-start time (both bindings here tie) and `id` is a random
    UUID, so which one wins is arbitrary — but it must be STABLE, not vary

    assert len(set(prompts)) == 1, "the grounding pipeline varied across repeated calls"

   with two enabled bindings (a real, supported shape; TriggerBinding's
   unique constraint is per-pipeline, not per-suite) could get either
   pipeline's cadence silently grounding the suggestion, varying by

**#1648 merged and closed.** Four of eleven W4 issues done now: #1644, #1513, #1632, #1648.

Per the priority order, next up is **#1635** (evidence-card enrichment), which I placed ahead of #1633 (RCA narrative) since it feeds richer input into that narrative. Given the scale of review each of these has required, want me to continue straight into #1635, or pause here for a status check?

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user asked me to: "Check the pending Items from week 4. research and plan the details. Check filled issues, create additional if required. rank them based on priority and dependencies. Create a TODO list, start the execution." with an explicit constraint: "note: keep the comments at minimum [~ 0.2 prose to code ratio]". This refers to DataQ's v1.2 Week 4 milestone ("LLM check suggestions + compliance G2"). After initial research and a priority ranking (presented to and implicitly accepted by the user), the user has been issuing brief "continue" signals to work through the ranked issue list sequentially, one PR at a time, with full CI verification and `/code-review` before each merge.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - DataQ's `LLMProvider` seam (ADR 0042): `KIND_BUILDERS`/`KIND_VALIDATORS` registries in `llm_service.py`, generic `execute_invocation` claim→build→validate→persist lifecycle, `LlmInvocation` model with statuses `pending|running|succeeded|failed`.
   - GX (Great Expectations) expectation types vs. monitor kinds (`freshness`, `volume`, `schema_drift`, `anomaly`) vs. `comparison` kind — three axes of check authoring (`kind`, `engine`, `dimension`).
   - `monitor_expectation_type(kind)` → `"monitor:<kind>"` canonical expectation_type string for monitor-kind checks.
   - Freshness monitor shape: `kind="freshness"`, `config={"column": ...}` (required for SQL-queryable connections), threshold is `fail_threshold`/`critical_threshold` (Decimal hours), NOT part of `config`.
   - PII/security posture: output validation is the security boundary (not prompt hygiene) — established in #1512/#1513/#1632.
   - G3 governance floor: warehouse tags + suite `column_policy` → masking of profile stats before they reach an LLM prompt (`live_probe.py` primitives).
   - `TriggerBinding`/`PipelineRun` models — orchestration domain; `TriggerBinding` unique constraint is `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env, suite_id)`, NOT unique per suite (a suite can have multiple enabled bindings).
   - #1199 near-miss machinery (`workspace_health_service.list_current_env_near_misses` / `orchestration_service.list_env_near_misses`): detects a suite's binding scoped to one env while its pipeline actually fires (successfully) in a different env with no binding there.
   - Postgres `now()` is transaction-start time, not per-statement — same-transaction rows can share identical `created_at` timestamps (a recurring gotcha across this session).
   - `gen_random_uuid()` for PK generation is random (UUIDv4), not time-ordered — cannot be used to infer "most recent" without a separate timestamp.
   - Mutation-verification discipline (project standing rule): every regression test claiming to catch a bug must be proven by reverting the fix and confirming the test fails for the right reason. Discovered mid-session that outcome-based/empirical tests can be fundamentally unable to detect certain defects (e.g., a missing `ORDER BY` when repeated queries against unchanged data return a stable physical order regardless) — such cases require structural tests (SQL-capture via `sqlalchemy.event.listen(engine, "before_cursor_execute", ...)`) instead.
   - `capture_logs()` from `structlog.testing` — established pattern (in `test_secrets.py`) for asserting on structlog output in a bare unit test (since `caplog` requires `configure_logging()` to have run).
   - GitHub review-thread merge-blocking: `gh pr merge` can fail with "base branch policy prohibits the merge" even with all CI green, due to an unresolved inline review thread (including automated CodeQL findings posted as PR review comments) — must resolve/fix and let it auto-resolve before merge succeeds.
   - `docs/progress.md` update convention: required per PR-template checkbox; do it within the same PR when possible; if `main`'s branch-protection hook blocks a direct commit and the update was missed, a separate follow-up PR is needed.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **#1644 (merged, PR #1716 + docs PR #1718):**
   - `backend/app/services/llm_service.py`: Added `reap_stuck_invocations()` (guarded conditional bulk UPDATE, not select-then-mutate) and refactored `execute_invocation()` to accumulate state in a local `terminal: dict` (never mutate the ORM object directly) and persist via a guarded `UPDATE ... WHERE id=... AND status='running'`, returning `"superseded"` when 0 rows affected (reaped out from under it). Added token-count logging on supersede.
   - `backend/app/core/config.py`: Added `llm_invocation_pending_threshold_minutes=15`, `llm_invocation_running_threshold_minutes=10`.
   - `backend/app/worker/tasks.py` / `celery_app.py`: New `reap_stuck_llm_invocations` task + 5-min beat schedule entry.
   - `backend/tests/services/test_llm_reaper.py`, `backend/tests/worker/test_llm_reaper_task.py`, additions to `test_llm_service.py` (e.g. `test_result_does_not_resurrect_a_row_the_reaper_already_closed_out`).
   - `.env.app.example`: added the two new threshold env vars.
   - Filed issue #1717 (missing index on `llm_invocations.status`) as non-blocking follow-up.

   **#1513 (merged):**
   - `backend/app/services/llm_prompt_context.py` (NEW): shared module — `target_identity()`, `list_columns_for_prompt()`, `masked_profile_for_prompt()` (returns `MaskedProfile(row_count, columns)`), `check_sql_target_preconditions()`. Created specifically to eliminate duplication found by review between `llm_sqlgen.py` and the new `llm_checksuggest.py`.
   - `backend/app/services/llm_checksuggest.py` (NEW): `CHECKSUGGEST_KIND="check_suggestion"`, `SUGGESTIBLE_EXPECTATION_TYPES`, `CHECKSUGGEST_SCHEMA`, `check_generation_preconditions`, `build_prompt`, `_validate_one`, `validate_output` — GX-suggestion-only at this point.
   - `backend/app/services/llm_sqlgen.py`: refactored to use the new shared `llm_prompt_context` module (removed its own `_target_identity`/inline masking logic).
   - `backend/app/core/jsonsafe.py`: Added a `bytes → value.hex()` branch to `sanitize_json` (fixes a driver-boundary gap found by review — raw bytes from a BINARY column's MIN/MAX would otherwise leak into an LLM prompt or crash JSONB serialization).
   - `backend/app/api/v1/llm.py`: Added `POST /llm/check_suggestions` route.
   - Tests: `backend/tests/services/test_llm_checksuggest.py`, `backend/tests/core/test_jsonsafe.py` additions, `backend/tests/services/test_profile_service.py` additions (`test_assemble_sanitizes_binary_min_max_and_top_values`).

   **#1632 (merged):**
   - `backend/tests/support/adversarial.py`: Added `PROMPT_INJECTION_STRINGS` list.
   - `backend/tests/services/test_llm_injection_battery.py` (NEW): column-name/top-value/range/table/schema slot injection tests, structural "no Result import" test (via `hasattr`), log-redaction test (via `capture_logs()`), parametrized across both LLM kinds.

   **#1648 (merged, PR #1738 — most recent work):**
   - `backend/app/services/orchestration_service.py`: Added `PipelineCadence` dataclass (`sample_count`, `insufficient_history`, `median_gap_hours`, `max_gap_hours`, `suggested_fail_threshold_hours`), `compute_pipeline_cadence()`, and `get_enabled_binding(session, suite_id)`:
     ```python
     def get_enabled_binding(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID) -> TriggerBinding | None:
         """... `id` breaks a `created_at` tie ... the tiebreak is
         stable-but-arbitrary, not truly "most recent" ..."""
         return session.scalars(
             select(TriggerBinding)
             .where(TriggerBinding.suite_id == suite_id, TriggerBinding.enabled.is_(True))
             .order_by(TriggerBinding.created_at.desc(), TriggerBinding.id.desc())
         ).first()
     ```
   - `backend/app/services/llm_checksuggest.py`: Extended with `FRESHNESS_EXPECTATION_TYPE`, `_build_schema(*, include_freshness: bool)` (schema is now built dynamically), `CHECKSUGGEST_SCHEMA = _build_schema(include_freshness=False)`, `_FRESHNESS_SYSTEM_ADDENDUM`, `_cadence_context()`, `_near_misses()`/`_coverage_warning_text()`, `_validate_freshness_suggestion()` with explicit finiteness check:
     ```python
     threshold_raw = raw.get("fail_threshold_hours")
     fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None
     if threshold_raw is not None:
         try:
             fail_threshold = Decimal(str(threshold_raw))
         except InvalidOperation:
             return None, "fail_threshold_hours must be a number"
         if not fail_threshold.is_finite():
             return None, "fail_threshold_hours must be a finite number"
     ```
     And the final fix (resolving the CodeQL unresolved-thread block on merge):
     ```python
     schema = _build_schema(include_freshness=True) if include_freshness else CHECKSUGGEST_SCHEMA
     return prompt, system, schema
     ```
     `validate_output` now also returns a deterministic `coverage_warnings` field, computed independently of the model's own output.
   - `backend/app/api/v1/suites.py`: Added `SuiteCadenceRead` Pydantic model and `GET /suites/{suite_id}/cadence` route (edit-gated), giving `suggested_fail_threshold_hours` a genuine consumer (resolving a "dead field" review finding).
   - Tests: `backend/tests/services/test_pipeline_cadence.py` (NEW, including the mutation-proof `test_get_enabled_binding_query_is_ordered` using SQL-capture via `sqlalchemy.event`), `backend/tests/services/test_llm_checksuggest_cadence.py` (NEW, extensive), additions to `backend/tests/api/test_suites.py` (`test_cadence_with_no_binding`, `test_cadence_with_a_bound_pipeline_and_regular_history`, `test_cadence_requires_edit_access`).
   - `docs/progress.md`: flipped #1648 to done with a detailed description, within the same PR.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **#1644 race condition (2 rounds)**: select-then-mutate had no WHERE-status guard → fixed with conditional bulk UPDATE; then found the SAME class of bug in `execute_invocation`'s own terminal write → fixed by never mutating the ORM object directly, using a local dict + guarded UPDATE instead. Both mutation-verified.
   - **#1513 duplication**: `llm_sqlgen.py` and `llm_checksuggest.py` hand-rolled the same profiling/masking pipeline with subtly different target-identity fields → extracted shared `llm_prompt_context.py` module.
   - **#1513 driver-boundary gap**: `sanitize_json` had no `bytes` handling → added `.hex()` branch, mutation-verified.
   - **#1513 silent no-op**: `validate_output`'s blank `connection_type=""` fallback silently defeated `reject_dataframe_only_expectation` → fixed by raising `LLMRequestInvalidError` immediately when suite/connection can't be resolved; required updating pre-existing tests that relied on the old permissive behavior.
   - **#1632 fragile test-double duplication and a fragile text-based structural check**: `_LogRecorder` reinvented `capture_logs()`; the "no Result import" check only inspected the first line of an import statement (defeated by a Black multi-line wrap) → replaced with `not hasattr(module, "Result")`.
   - **#1648 NaN/Infinity crash**: `Decimal(str(nan_or_inf))` doesn't raise, but the subsequent `< 0` comparison on NaN raises an UNCAUGHT `decimal.InvalidOperation` that sinks the entire suggestion batch (verified empirically via direct Python REPL testing). Fixed with `.is_finite()` check. Mutation-verified (confirmed the exact uncaught-exception traceback against the reverted code).
   - **#1648 non-determinism, and MY OWN test design error**: my first regression test (`test_two_enabled_bindings_pick_stays_stable_across_calls`, calling `build_prompt` 5x and checking for identical output) did NOT actually catch the missing-`ORDER BY` mutation, because Postgres returns a stable physical row order for repeated queries against unchanged data within one transaction regardless of whether an ORDER BY clause exists. I caught this myself by explicitly re-running the "passing" test against the reverted (unordered) code 5 times and observing it kept passing — this was an important self-correction. Rewrote the test to inspect the compiled SQL directly via a `sqlalchemy.event.listen(engine, "before_cursor_execute", ...)` hook, asserting `"ORDER BY"` appears in the captured statement — this version WAS successfully mutation-verified.
   - **#1648 dead field discovered via unresolved CodeQL thread blocking merge**: `gh pr merge` failed with "base branch policy prohibits the merge" despite all CI green; GraphQL query revealed an unresolved CodeQL review comment: "The global variable 'CHECKSUGGEST_SCHEMA' is not used." Verified via grep this was accurate (only referenced in a test file, never read in production code since `build_prompt` always called `_build_schema()` fresh). 1	"""The deterministic incident evidence card (ADR 0034 decision 4 / Theme-2 layer 1)."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import uuid
6	from collections.abc import Callable
7	from datetime import UTC, datetime
8	from decimal import Decimal
9	from typing import Any
10	
11	from sqlalchemy import func, select
12	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
13	
14	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
15	from backend.app.db.models import ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS, Asset, Check, PipelineRun, Result, Run
16	from backend.app.lineage.edges import downstream_assets
17	
18	log = get_logger(__name__)
19	
20	# How many recent metric readings the trend layer carries, and how many prior
21	# pipeline runs the delay-vs-history baseline averages over.
22	_TREND_LIMIT = 10
23	_PIPELINE_HISTORY_LIMIT = 10
24	
25	# The list-valued, sample-row-bearing keys of `gx_runner._SAMPLE_KEYS` — the two that carry raw cell
26	# values (vs. the scalar `unexpected_count`/`unexpected_percent` aggregates).
27	_SAMPLE_LIST_KEYS = frozenset({"partial_unexpected_list", "unexpected_index_list"})
28	
29	
30	def _layer(name: str, fn: Callable[[], Any]) -> Any:
31	    """Run one evidence layer best-effort: any failure logs a structured warning
32	    and degrades that layer to ``None`` — never poisoning the card (and through
33	    it the whole run's incident sync).
34	    """
35	    try:
36	        return fn()
37	    except Exception:
38	        log.warning("incident_evidence_layer_failed", layer=name)
39	        return None
40	
41	
42	def _num(value: Decimal | None) -> float | None:
43	    """Widen a NUMERIC metric to a JSON-friendly float (``None`` stays ``None``)."""
44	    return float(value) if value is not None else None
45	
46	
47	def _iso(value: datetime | None) -> str | None:
48	    return value.isoformat() if value is not None else None
49	
50	
51	def build_evidence(
52	    session: Session,
53	    *,
54	    run: Run,
55	    result: Result,
56	    check: Check | None,
57	    asset: Asset | None,
58	) -> dict[str, Any]:
59	    """Assemble the layer-1 evidence card for a breaching ``result`` on ``run``."""
60	    return {
61	        "generated_at": _utc_now_iso(),
62	        "check": _layer("check", lambda: _check_layer(check)),
63	        "asset": _layer("asset", lambda: _asset_layer(asset)),
64	        "failing_result": _layer("failing_result", lambda: _failing_result_layer(result)),
65	        "metric_trend": _layer(
66	            "metric_trend", lambda: _metric_trend_layer(session, check_id=result.check_id)
67	        ),
68	        "sibling_checks": _layer(
69	            "sibling_checks",
70	            lambda: _sibling_checks_layer(session, run=run, exclude_check_id=result.check_id),
71	        ),
72	        "upstream_pipeline_run": _layer(
73	            "upstream_pipeline_run", lambda: _upstream_pipeline_layer(session, run=run)
74	        ),
75	        "downstream_blast_radius": _layer(
76	            "downstream_blast_radius", lambda: _blast_radius_layer(session, asset=asset)
77	        ),
78	        # Needs a live datasource profile of both batches — not existing data, not
79	        # cheap. Documented null placeholder (see module docstring).
80	        "profile_diff": None,
81	    }
82	
83	
84	def _utc_now_iso() -> str:
85	    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
86	
87	
88	def _check_layer(check: Check | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
89	    if check is None:
90	        return None
91	    return {
92	        "id": str(check.id),
93	        "name": check.name,
94	        "expectation_type": check.expectation_type,
95	        "kind": check.kind,
96	    }
97	
98	
99	def _asset_layer(asset: Asset | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
100	    if asset is None:
101	        return None
102	    return {
103	        "id": str(asset.id),
104	        "namespace": asset.namespace,
105	        "name": asset.name,
106	        "env": asset.env,
107	    }
108	
109	
110	def _failing_result_layer(result: Result) -> dict[str, Any]:
111	    """The breaching result — status + metric + GX aggregates. **No sample rows.**
112	    ``sample_failures`` is never read.
113	    """
114	    return {
115	        "status": result.status,
116	        "metric_value": _num(result.metric_value),
117	        "observed_value": _strip_sample_lists(result.observed_value),
118	        "expected_value": result.expected_value,
119	    }
120	
121	
122	def _strip_sample_lists(observed: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
123	    """Drop the list-valued sample-bearing keys from an ``observed_value`` dict
124	    (see ``_SAMPLE_LIST_KEYS``); non-dict / ``None`` shapes pass through.
125	    """
126	    if not isinstance(observed, dict):
127	        return observed
128	    return {key: val for key, val in observed.items() if key not in _SAMPLE_LIST_KEYS}
129	
130	
131	def _metric_trend_layer(session: Session, *, check_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
132	    """The last ``_TREND_LIMIT`` readings for the check (newest first) — the
133	    ``metric_value`` trend that distinguishes a sudden break from a slow drift.
134	    """
135	    rows = session.execute(
136	        select(Result.status, Result.metric_value, Result.created_at, Result.run_id)
137	        .where(Result.check_id == check_id)
138	        .order_by(Result.created_at.desc())
139	        .limit(_TREND_LIMIT)
140	    ).all()
141	    return [
142	        {
143	            "status": status,
144	            "metric_value": _num(metric_value),
145	            "created_at": _iso(created_at),
146	            "run_id": str(run_id),
147	        }
148	        for status, metric_value, created_at, run_id in rows
149	    ]
150	
151	
152	def _sibling_checks_layer(
153	    session: Session, *, run: Run, exclude_check_id: uuid.UUID
154	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
155	    """The other checks' outcomes in the same run (context: is the asset broadly
156	    unhealthy or is this one check the outlier?). Names via a single join.
157	    """
158	    rows = session.execute(
159	        select(Check.name, Result.status)
160	        .join(Check, Check.id == Result.check_id)
161	        .where(Result.run_id == run.id, Result.check_id != exclude_check_id)
162	        .order_by(Check.name)
163	    ).all()
164	    return [{"check_name": name, "status": status} for name, status in rows]
165	
166	
167	def _upstream_pipeline_layer(session: Session, *, run: Run) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
168	    """The orchestration pipeline run that triggered this suite run, + its delay
169	    vs. that pipeline's own history.
170	    """
171	    marker = run.triggered_by
172	    if not marker:
173	        return None
174	    provider, sep, _rest = marker.partition(":")
175	    if not sep or provider not in ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS:
176	        return None
177	    # Reconstruct-and-compare, not parse-and-split: `provider_run_id` (e.g. an
178	    # Airflow DAG run's default `run_id`, "manual__2026-08-08T01:30:00+00:00")
179	    # can itself contain colons, so there is no reliable place to cut the
180	    # "<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>" marker to recover it
181	    # (a trailing `rpartition(":")` used to truncate it to a few characters,
182	    # #1713). `orchestration_service._trigger_suites` builds the marker as
183	    # `f"{provider}:{pipeline_or_dag_id}:{provider_run_id}"`, so inverting it by
184	    # equality against the stored PipelineRun columns recovers the SAME row the
185	    # marker was built from. It does NOT prove that row is the only one that
186	    # could produce this string: dbt's `pipeline_or_dag_id` (job_name) is
187	    # free-form webhook input with no colon restriction, so two distinct rows
188	    # can reconstruct to an identical marker if a colon lands differently
189	    # across their pipeline/run-id boundary. `.all()` + the count check below
190	    # catches that rather than letting `.first()` silently attribute the
191	    # incident's evidence to whichever row Postgres happens to return first.
192	    candidates = session.scalars(
193	        select(PipelineRun).where(
194	            PipelineRun.provider == provider,
195	            func.concat(
196	                PipelineRun.provider,
197	                ":",
198	                PipelineRun.pipeline_or_dag_id,
199	                ":",
200	                PipelineRun.provider_run_id,
201	            )
202	            == marker,
203	        )
204	    ).all()
205	    if len(candidates) != 1:
206	        if candidates:
207	            log.warning(
208	                "upstream_pipeline_marker_ambiguous",
209	                marker=marker,
210	                provider=provider,
211	                candidate_count=len(candidates),
212	            )
213	        return None
214	    pipeline_run = candidates[0]
215	    return {
216	        "provider": pipeline_run.provider,
217	        "pipeline_or_dag_id": pipeline_run.pipeline_or_dag_id,
218	        "provider_run_id": pipeline_run.provider_run_id,
219	        "status": pipeline_run.status,
220	        "started_at": _iso(pipeline_run.started_at),
221	        "finished_at": _iso(pipeline_run.finished_at),
222	        "duration_seconds": _duration_seconds(pipeline_run),
223	        "delay_seconds_vs_history": _delay_vs_history(session, pipeline_run),
224	    }
225	
226	
227	def _duration_seconds(pipeline_run: PipelineRun) -> float | None:
228	    if pipeline_run.started_at is None or pipeline_run.finished_at is None:
229	        return None
230	    return (pipeline_run.finished_at - pipeline_run.started_at).total_seconds()
231	
232	
233	def _delay_vs_history(session: Session, pipeline_run: PipelineRun) -> float | None:
234	    """This pipeline run's duration minus the average of its recent prior succeeded
235	    runs — positive = slower than usual. ``None`` when either duration or the
236	    baseline (needs ≥1 prior completed run) is unavailable (skip gracefully).
237	    """
238	    this_duration = _duration_seconds(pipeline_run)
239	    if this_duration is None:
240	        return None
241	    prior = session.execute(
242	        select(PipelineRun.started_at, PipelineRun.finished_at)
243	        .where(
244	            PipelineRun.provider == pipeline_run.provider,
245	            PipelineRun.pipeline_or_dag_id == pipeline_run.pipeline_or_dag_id,
246	            PipelineRun.id != pipeline_run.id,
247	            PipelineRun.status == "succeeded",
248	            PipelineRun.started_at.is_not(None),
249	            PipelineRun.finished_at.is_not(None),
250	            PipelineRun.created_at < pipeline_run.created_at,
251	        )
252	        .order_by(PipelineRun.created_at.desc())
253	        .limit(_PIPELINE_HISTORY_LIMIT)
254	    ).all()
255	    durations = [float((fin - start).total_seconds()) for start, fin in prior]
256	    if not durations:
257	        return None
258	    baseline = sum(durations) / len(durations)
259	    return this_duration - baseline
260	
261	
262	def _blast_radius_layer(session: Session, *, asset: Asset | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
263	    """The downstream assets reachable from the failing one (lineage §2) — the
264	    "what breaks downstream" answer. Empty when the asset is unknown or a lineage
265	    leaf; ``downstream_assets`` is itself depth-capped + cycle-safe.
266	    """
267	    if asset is None:
268	        return []
269	    return [
270	        {"id": str(a.id), "namespace": a.namespace, "name": a.name, "env": a.env}
271	        for a in downstream_assets(session, asset.id)
272	    ]

66	    if role == ADMIN:
